# Introduction

QC the integrated object (AnoCar V3)

# QC metrics
nFeature = 500, percent.mt = 5

```{r}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,      # hide code (so md shows only text + plots)
  message = FALSE,   # suppress messages
  warning = FALSE    # suppress warnings
)
```

```{r}
library(Seurat)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(cowplot)
library(tidyr)
```


# read in integrated object and number of cells
```{r}
obj <- readRDS("/project2/aealmada_561/judyz/20260621_scRNA_lizard/rds/integrated_obj_nfeat500_mt5_anocarV3.rds")
obj
```

# check RNA QC metrics

```{r fig.width=6, fig.height=3}
VlnPlot(obj, features = "nFeature_RNA", group.by = "orig.ident", pt.size = 0) + NoLegend()
VlnPlot(obj, features = "nCount_RNA", group.by = "orig.ident", pt.size = 0) + NoLegend()
VlnPlot(obj, features = "percent.mt", group.by = "orig.ident", pt.size = 0) + NoLegend()
```


by seurat clusters

```{r fig.width=10, fig.height=3}
VlnPlot(obj, features = "nFeature_RNA", group.by = "seurat_clusters", pt.size = 0) + NoLegend()
VlnPlot(obj, features = "nCount_RNA", group.by = "seurat_clusters", pt.size = 0) + NoLegend()
VlnPlot(obj, features = "percent.mt", group.by = "seurat_clusters", pt.size = 0) + NoLegend()
```

cluster 15 is a low-qual cluster? if lack of a clear marker genes we can just drop

```{r fig.width=15, fig.height=6}
FeaturePlot(obj, features=c("percent.mt", "nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA"), ncol=3, reduction="tsne", order=TRUE, raster=F)
```


# Check integration and potential batch effect
```{r fig.width=15, fig.height=6}
p1 <- DimPlot(obj, reduction="tsne", group.by = "orig.ident", raster=F) + NoLegend()
p2 <- DimPlot(obj, reduction="tsne", group.by = "seurat_clusters", label=T, raster=F) + NoLegend()
p1 + p2
```


## cells per library passed initial qc
```{r fig.width=3, fig.height=4}
cell_counts <- as.data.frame(table(obj$orig.ident))
colnames(cell_counts) <- c("orig.ident", "count")
# bar plot
ggplot(cell_counts, aes(x = orig.ident, y = count)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_text(aes(label=count), vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    title = "Number of Cells per Library",
    x = "Library",
    y = "Cell Count"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

# Library composition per seurat clusters (barplots)
no batch effect, every seurat cluster is well represented by both samples

```{r}
cell_counts <- obj@meta.data %>% 
  group_by(seurat_clusters, orig.ident) %>% 
  summarise(cell_n = n(), .groups = "drop")

cell_props <- cell_counts %>%
  group_by(seurat_clusters) %>% 
  mutate(prop = cell_n / sum(cell_n))

ggplot(cell_props, aes(x = as.factor(seurat_clusters), y = prop, fill = orig.ident)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Seurat Cluster", y = "Proportion of Cells", fill = "Sample") +
  ggtitle("Proportion of each sample within each seurat cluster")
```

# Visualize cell type specific marker genes
## FAP 1 and FAP 2

```{r fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
genes <- c("pdgfra", "mfap5", "pcolce2", "postn", "pdgfrb")

FeaturePlot(obj, features=genes, reduction="tsne", ncol = 3, order=TRUE)
```

```{r fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
for (gene in genes) {
  print(VlnPlot(obj, features = gene, group.by = "seurat_clusters", pt.size = 0))
}
```
